The pure class interface. 
public class ArraySeq<A>
  extends Seq<A>
Implementation variant of sequences using arrays as the internal representation.

This variant of sequences is nearly as fast as Pizza/Java arrays, as far as index-based operations are concerned. Methods such as insertion and slicing are relative fast, since they are realized by the native array method System.arraycopy.

Storage economy is as for arrays (no ``holes'' in the representing array). However, array sequences of primitive objects such as booleans have to be expected to be stored as Java arrays of their boxed counterparts, unless they are constructed from a given array of primitives.

ArraySeq

public ArraySeq(A[] array);
Construct a sequence from an array. The array is embedded by reference into the array sequence, that is becomes its internal representation. The effect of later indirect updates on the given array is not specified.

ArraySeq

public ArraySeq(int size,
                (int) -> A f);
Construct a sequence of given size which contains at the the ith element the result of calling f(i).

from
public static <A> Seq<A> from(Aggregate<A> other);
Construct a array sequence which contains the enumerated elements of another aggregate. This static method is optimized according to the actual representation of the other aggregate. In particular, if the other aggregate is an array sequence again, it is simply returned.
